current.text: He is a projected starter at forward next to Acuff, LaVine, Hunter and Sabonis. Nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot.
DeRozan, Westbrook and Schroder are no longer on the Kings. LaVine and Sabonis remain.

Experts disagree on his usage. Josh and the power forward rankings expect more usage and big minutes now that the Kings cleared out shots. Lloyd sees him as about the third option behind LaVine and Sabonis, with no big usage jump, no 20 points a game and a heavy defensive load.
Experts doubt his 1.6 blocks per game from last season will hold, and doubt his shooting will return.
If he reaches about 20 percent usage and shoots better, he can easily beat his draft spot.
Josh is happy to take him in round 10 and expects about a top 100 season. Pick 93 is too early in a regular draft, and ESPN's rank of 83 is too high. An ADP of about 122 is too late.
He is 26 and in the first year of a 5-year, 140 million USD contract.
Ham says this is the season he has to prove himself.
The Kings may still trade Sabonis or LaVine, the two players who limit his usage.
The Kings are projected near the bottom of the league, with Vegas at about 21.5 to 22.5 wins. Experts disagree on whether they will sit veterans or keep trying to win to avoid the relegation zone.

durable.text: He is a better category league player than points league player.
A finger injury early and an ankle injury late cost him most of the 2025-26 season.
He has made big strides as a defender and rebounder. In a small sample he blocked many shots and defended well.
The shooting from his rookie season has not come back.

note: Both sites value him at 4 USD, his average cost is only 1.0 to 1.4 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. With a Yahoo rank of 99 and an ESPN rank of 83, he is a cheap late target worth 1 to 4 USD as a round 10 forward. No category is flagged weak, so he fits any build, with threes, blocks and few turnovers making up for a soft 44 FG% and 1.6 assists. Early in the season, check whether his blocks stay near 1 per game (not the 1.6 he posted in only 23 games last season), whether his FG% gets back to 44 to 45, and whether a Sabonis or LaVine trade gives him more shots.
